subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` as the canonical all-configured-model health check, or fold that behavior into a broader model-safety workflow first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent CLI surface makes live provider calls and overlaps fallback-chain testing, staged migration, rate-limit visibility, and auth-provider diagnostics.

options.title: Approve status probe all-mode
options.body: Add an opt-in `models status --probe --all` mode with explicit live-call warnings, bounded concurrency, documented JSON fields, and focused unit plus redacted real CLI proof.

options.title: Fold into broader model safety
options.body: Keep this issue open as part of a unified staged migration and fallback-chain diagnostic design before adding new CLI flags.

options.title: Defer core surface
options.body: Leave current auth probes unchanged and rely on manual provider-specific checks until maintainers want to own live all-model diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Approve status probe all-mode
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in `models status --probe --all` mode with explicit live-call warnings, bounded concurrency, documented JSON fields, and focused unit plus redacted real CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history on model status/probe behavior and already appears in prior review context for the overlapping diagnostics work.
